title: A 0.1 percent added weight kept sampled source residuals below 0.54 percent in two partial adult worm models
abstract: We tested whether one missing electrical link gives useful source separation in passive models of two partial adult C. elegans maps. Seven exact twin pairs gave 2,004 pair-endpoint cases per setting. Every positive added exterior link breaks exact rank-one ambiguity. At an added weight of 0.1 percent of original source exterior weight, all sampled relative residuals stayed below 0.54 percent after unknown complex amplitude was fitted. At a 1 percent weight, 88.73 and 87.15 percent of cases in the two maps exceeded a 1 percent residual benchmark. A 10 percent source capacitance difference changed little. Direct solves and synthetic graphs checked the edge update. A denser sampled grid gave no benchmark changes in 80 selected setting-cases. Exact rank can change while response separation stays small. Hypothetical links, assumed circuit parameters, full remote observation, relative signal scaling and absent activity data prevent biological or noise-rate claims. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and external regeneration steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Minimum and maximum sampled residuals across absent-edge placements, and the fraction above the 1 percent benchmark. Added weights and capacitances are model assumptions.
